items.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025
items.q: we used to have to imitate Bach chorales and things like that so I was very familiar.

ctx.x: Well I went to Curtis so I grew up writing. You know we used to have to imitate Bach chorales and things like that so I was very familiar. But then that whole pop music scene in Philadelphia in the '60s and '70s overwhelmingly fascinated me. You know I mean because they were kids who grew up in my neighborhood after the great songwriters and the great arrangers and the great everybody and it just fascinated me. I went a little different left, I went to Curtis as a cello player but yet participated in Cameo and…

I don't want to make too much out of this but it seems to me when you were making this decision at 17 according to your promo here, that you had one foot in the white world of music and you had another in the black world of music. Were you aware of that? Was that partly your decision to go — to leave Curtis and go in this other direction?
